f-iter004-001's DEPTH removal lands 76 days late: 0628c398a4 (2026-10-30) deleted 18 DEPTH lines from sk-prompt/SKILL.md, so the v4.0.0.0 note was accurate at its own tag and every v4.0.0.x release still shipped DEPTH, while the sk-prompt packet changelog documented the removal at v4.0.0.0; the defect class is a skill changelog describing a refactor that had not landed, which a reader can lose against git. The v4 line inherited these hub defects rather than introducing them: 13 of the 30 attributable code-level findings predate v4.0.0.0-beta.1, 6 shipped exactly at v4.0.0.0 and 5 arrived later in the line, because the .opencode to .skilled rename 330427cf30 (2026-09-17) rewrote paths without rewriting content, so every stale count, wrong relative link and no-op flag crossed the boundary intact; a release audit reading only a path-limited diff across that rename sees every line changed and nothing reviewed, which is why -S with --follow is the required instrument. Verify: git log --follow -S'21 forms' shows cdc8e7192d 2026-09-04 while git log --follow -S'--benchmark-id' shows 27e91daa10 2026-07-15, both surviving 330427cf30 unchanged.

label: The research append gateway validates iteration status against a six-value enum (complete, error, insight, stuck, thought, timeout) and, on any other word, exits 1 with the single line {"ok":false,"phase":"runtime","reason":"Payload validator rejected the event","code":"RUNTIME_ERROR"} naming neither the offending field nor the allowed values; a status of "attribution" produced exactly that, and the only way to find the requirement was to read ITERATION_COMPLETION_STATUS_RULE in the schema source. Verify: node append-mode-event.cjs --mode research --run-directory <run> --event-json <record with status:"attribution"> returns exit 1 and that message.

The gateway's legacy deep-research upcaster maps a free-form iteration status into the enum without normalising it, so an out-of-vocabulary word is refused rather than coerced, and the refusal is reported at phase runtime rather than as a payload_missing/unknown_field error that names the field
